question.text: For an open-ended Category III AIF, what is the MINIMUM regulatory frequency of NAV disclosure to investors?

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI (AIF) Regulations per the chapter: 'NAV calculated on each Valuation Day shall be disclosed to all investors on a quarterly basis for closed-ended AIFs and on a monthly basis for open-ended AIFs.' Cat III funds investing only in listed securities 'usually' compute daily, but the minimum disclosure frequency is monthly (open-ended) / quarterly (closed-ended). The Trap: Daily is typical practice when investing in listed securities but NOT the regulatory minimum. Quarterly applies to closed-ended Cat III, not open-ended. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C mandates the same. Cross-Exam Context: Cat I/II uses quarterly/semi-annual valuation (XIX-D/XIX-A) - Cat III is stricter. Manager's Pro-Tip: In practice, prime-broker files and exchange feeds let Cat III funds compute daily NAV cheaply; investor statements may still go monthly, but MTM for margining is daily. Document the computation-vs-disclosure frequency distinction in the PPM.
